subject: dsa
title: Meeting Rooms II
summary: The minimum number of rooms equals the maximum number of meetings happening at the same instant. Sweep the timeline; a room frees up when a meeting ends and can be reused later.
problem: Given meeting time intervals, find the minimum number of rooms required to hold them all.

steps.caption: Find the fewest rooms so no two overlapping meetings share one. That equals the most meetings overlapping at any moment.
[0,30] starts, so one room is in use.
At time 5, [5,10] begins while [0,30] is still running. They overlap, so a second room is needed.
[5,10] ends at 10, freeing its room for a later meeting.
[15,20] starts after 10, so it reuses the freed room. No third room is needed.
The peak overlap was 2 meetings, so 2 rooms suffice. The answer is 2.
